notes:
Account summary
- Enterprise prospect in payments. Primary concern is Dedicated capacity predictability: lead times for new pools + expansions, and strong 'ready' gating so no traffic hits a partially configured pool.
- They run tightly controlled change-management (CAB) and require a written plan for any infra change (including GPU expansion), plus measurable validation and rollback points.

Key requirements (from calls + emails)
- Capacity lead time:
  - Wants a committed expansion SLA by region/SKU (not just a target). Quote from call: "We can't tell our product teams 'maybe next week'—we need dates."
  - Asked for p50/p95 historical time-to-ready and what levers improve it.
  - Wants a breakdown of steps (provisioning, imaging, bootstrap, validation) and ownership/escalation per step.
- Readiness validation (hard gate before routing):
  - Must run GPU health checks (ECC, thermals), networking/DNS/TLS checks, runtime smoke test, and a minimal throughput/latency canary.
  - Wants pass/fail criteria and what happens on failure (auto-replace vs manual intervention).
  - Explicitly asked that routing never sees capacity in intermediate states (Provisioning/Imaging/Bootstrapping/Validating).
- Change management / controls:
  - Needs a formal runbook + rollback plan, ideally with stage-level checkpoints and audit trails.
  - Requested ability to pause/resume automation runs during maintenance windows, with an audit log of who took action and why.
  - Wants notification templates for planned expansions and incident-style updates if a run fails.
- Security/compliance:
  - Image provenance: signed artifacts, documented promotion path for golden images, and pinned driver/runtime versions.
  - Audit logging: provisioning actions + config override ("break glass") must be logged and reviewable.
  - Data/control requirements: VPC deployment preferred; residency needed in US initially; EU might follow.

Current scope discussed
- Initial: Dedicated (VPC) with 2 pools (staging + prod). They expect at least 1 planned expansion within the first 60 days post-signature.
- Workloads: support-agent + summarization; moderate streaming usage. Latency sensitive for interactive support flows; cost sensitivity is secondary to reliability/predictability.

What we told them (positioning / commitments in progress)
- We are implementing provision-to-ready automation to reduce time-to-ready and make steps measurable/repeatable (stage metrics + dashboards).
- 'Ready' will be a control-plane state with explicit validation gates; routing will only advertise Ready pools.
- We can provide a change plan template and runbook-style sequence for CAB approval; follow-up will include a sample rollout checklist and readiness output format.

Open questions from prospect
- Exact time-to-ready SLA we will contract for new pools vs expansions (and whether it varies by region/SKU).
- Whether they can get a customer-facing view (or at least periodic updates) of stage progress during a bring-up.
- Log retention options for provisioning events and audit logs (duration + export).

Internal notes
- This account is effectively blocked on our ability to operationalize and credibly message: lead time + readiness gating + auditability.
- Recommend mapping our internal provisioning stages to their CAB steps; provide a concise document: "Dedicated Capacity Expansion Change Plan" with validation, rollback points, and escalation paths.
